title: ITR filing deadline for audited taxpayers ends today for FY26: What if you file taxes late? - Bhaskar English
text:
ITR Filing Deadline India: Last Date for Audited Taxpayers | Avoid Penalty Get the latest news from your city
 Download Sat, Nov 21, 2026 Updated 08:54 PM IST ITR filing deadline for audited taxpayers ends today for FY26: What are consequences of missing the cutoff?
 10 hours ago Loading advertisement... Credit: Pexels Credit: Pexels To Read Bhaskar English… Better News Experience Read in App In the Browser Continue Saturday, 21 November, 2026, marks the final deadline for taxpayers whose accounts are subject to audit to file their Income Tax Returns (ITR) for Assessment Year (AY) 2026–27. Financial advisors and tax professionals across the country are urging eligible corporate entities, working partners of audited firms, and high-income businesses to submit their returns before midnight to avoid steep financial penalties and legal complications.
 Loading advertisement... Who Is The Deadline For? 
 The November 21 deadline specifically applies to businesses, corporate entities, and individual taxpayers required to submit tax audit reports under Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act. While non-audited individual taxpayers completed their filings earlier in the financial cycle, today’s deadline represents the main compliance hurdle for India’s corporate sector for Financial Year 2025–26.
 Tax experts note that compliance rates have been steady, though a significant volume of last-minute filings is expected through the final hours of the day.
 Loading advertisement... Consequences of Missing the Cutoff 
 Failing to meet tonight’s deadline carries immediate financial repercussions:
 Late Fees: Non-filers attract mandatory penalties under Section 234F—up to ₹5,000 for taxpayers with total income exceeding ₹5 lakh, and ₹1,000 for those below that threshold.
 Penal Interest: A statutory interest rate of 1% per month (or part of a month) under Section 234A will be levied on the unpaid tax liability from the original due date.
 Loss of Business Carry-Forward Benefits: Delaying filing past today forfeits the right to carry forward current-year business losses and capital losses to set off against future income, potentially increasing future tax exposure.
 Tax consultants report high traffic volumes on the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) e-filing portal. Authorities recommend that taxpayers double-check their Form 26AS, Annual Information Statement (AIS), and Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS) for discrepancies before clicking submit.
 What If You Miss The Deadline? 
 To complete the filing process, taxpayers must ensure their returns are digitally signed (DSC) or e-verified immediately using Aadhaar OTP or net banking. Taxpayers who miss tonight’s deadline will only have until December 31, 2026, to file a belated return, subject to the applicable fines and interest.
